newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-BRAZILIANS LEAD QUALIFYING FOR LONG BEACH RACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BRAZILIANS LEAD QUALIFYING FOR LONG BEACH RACE.

text.p: Brazilians Gil de Ferran and Mauricio Gugelmin led the provisional qualifiers Friday for Sunday's Long Beach Grand Prix CART IndyCar race.

De Ferran, last year's pole-sitter, broke his own lap record with a time of 51.293 seconds for an average speed of 111.313 mph (179.214) in a Reynard Honda on the 1.59-mile (2.56-km), eight-turn temporary road course.
Last year he won the pole with a time of 52.208 seconds for Jim Hall Racing. He switched to Walker Racing for this year.

After crashing last week with Christian Fittipaldi at Surfers Paradise, Australia, de Ferran's new team had a big job getting ready for this qualifying session. "It was a tough week for the guys who had to rebuild the car after our accident," de Ferran said.

"We took a little bit from what we learned last year," said de Ferran. "We took a little from what we learned at Australia last week and what we learned in winter testing, put it in cup, shook it up and ended up with a set-up that suits my driving style."
Formula One veteran Gugelmin, driving a Reynard Mercedes-Benz, was slightly off the pace at 51.745 seconds followed by Italian Allessandro Zanardi at 51.843 in a Reynard Honda.

Zanardi has a six-race pole-sitting streak at stake but expressed no concern over possibly ending the streak. "It's not a worry," the Italian said. "It will happen eventually but it's not a guarantee it will happen tomorrow."
Qualifying for Sunday's 105-lap, 167-mile (268-km) race concludes on Saturday.
